The ship gate proves Jolt and box3d expose the same methods -- it has never proved they agree on the same physics, and box3d cannot be run where this engine is developed, so the question can only be settled here, on your machine. pages.t: SweK Physics — Bayesian inference on HMC
pages.d: HMC as an inference instrument: fit a noisy oscillator's (A, omega) by rolling trajectories over the log-posterior. Two keys grade it — an exact conjugate posterior (algebra, not another chain) and frequentist CALIBRATION: over repeated fresh datasets the 90% interval must cover the known truth ~90% of the time. The sabotage understates the noise: every posterior looks tighter and better, and the coverage counter is the only place the failure is visible.

Two exact keys from one discretisation that fail in different ways. Static: the tip deflection is exactly FL^3/3EI. Dynamic: the vibration frequencies are roots of cos(b)cosh(b) = -1, so the ratios 6.2669 and 17.5475 are irrational numbers no plausible bug produces by accident. A tenfold stiffness change moves the deflection tenfold and leaves every ratio bit-identical, which is why one key cannot replace the other.

A blobulator kept as an avatar. Oddly normal, either or both -- Avataro / Avatarina / both, a palette you toggle. It breathes when idle and reacts when you tap: dance, rotate head, high-five, wave, nod, bounce. Reactions displace its metaballs and blend cumulatively -- stack a few and it makes an emergent shape rather than a canned animation, because metaballs merge by nature. Drag to orbit, pinch to zoom. This is the reactive core; a GPU-brain driver and a threat-tentacle-with-fire tip come next.

A blob that is genuinely held down. Gravity pulls, buoyancy exists only while it is hot, heat exists only while it spends energy, and energy only returns while it is not spending -- so hovering is never free and it has to bob for its altitude. The lava lamp was never unbound by gravity; a lamp IS buoyancy against gravity. What it lacked was choice. Here a seeded perceptron (or the GPU brain when connected) decides when to burn and when to coast, and the height is earned: doing nothing falls, burning flat out reaches but cannot hold, and the brain holds three times longer on the same tank. The skin tells the truth -- it glows lava when it is working and freezes to ice when it gives up -- and the wormhole gauge reads its energy.

Avataro and a herd of blobs, each with its own mind -- the same driver that runs the avatar runs every one of them, so they roam, keep their distance, and each picks its own moves on its own schedule. Because metaballs merge by summing, they bond with each other as well as with the host, and the count in the corner is the honest one: how many creatures you SEE is the number of connected components of the merge graph, not how many exist. Two bond, you see one. They part, you see two. Drag to orbit, pinch to zoom.

A blobulator's idea of a selfie: it casts its own X-ray shadows and is rebuilt from them, with nothing simulated anywhere. A metaball's shadow is closed-form -- for Wyvill's kernel it collapses to a single term, (32/35)*A*R*u^3.5, verified against brute-force integration to 4e-15. So the sinogram is written down exactly and back-projection must find the wax from those shadows alone. Getting here took two real failures worth more than the page: the blobulator's own kernel decays as 1/d-squared and never reaches zero, so filtered back-projection had no compact support and was biased by 108% no matter how many angles it got; truncating the kernel fixed that and introduced a hard edge, which rings. Wyvill's kernel is compact AND smooth, and the reconstruction lands at six hundredths of a percent -- better than the medical phantom, which is pinned near 14% forever because a head has edges.

Metaballs hit by a real shockwave. The blast is not an animation curve and not a radial fudge -- it is the compressible Euler equations, solved by the same module that earned a strong shock compressing gas by exactly 6.003 against Rankine-Hugoniot, conserves mass to seven parts in a quadrillion, and reproduces Sedov's blast radius law. The blobs do not know a shock is coming. They are simply dragged by the gas velocity at their own position, so when the front arrives they get shoved -- and the front's radius, measured live off the page's own density field, follows the Sedov law it was checked against. Nothing here is scripted: the wave arrives when the physics says it arrives.

Blobs that want the gauges but can never leave the stage. Each one is drawn to whichever instrument is nearest, so the gauges become the reason to be somewhere and the stage sorts itself into camps. They still have to earn every inch of altitude -- gravity pulls, buoyancy only exists while they are hot, heat only while they spend, and each is flown by the trained policy that learned to hold a height better than a hand-tuned controller. The walls are an invariant, not a force: containment clamps after integration, so nothing tunnels out no matter how hard it is shoved. They lean on the glass instead.

The Ising critical temperature by Binder cumulant against Fisher amplitude-ratio; the trap's free-energy difference by Jarzynski against Crooks; the LBM's viscosity as configured against what the fluid's shear waves actually do. pages.t: EV cosmic map -- a galaxy you can verify

pages.d: The large-scale structure of the universe, grown rather than drawn. It starts as a Gaussian random field carrying a prescribed power spectrum -- and that field is checked: build it to P(k) = k^-2, measure the spectrum back out, and it returns what was asked for to about four percent on well-sampled shells. Then Zel'dovich (1970): every parcel of matter coasts along its initial impulse, x = q + D*Psi(q), and filaments, sheets and voids fall out of nothing but that. The displacement solves Poisson in Fourier space to machine precision, and the moment a sheet folds on itself -- a caustic, the seed of every cluster here -- lands where the mathematics says it must, at D = 1/A. Drag the slider and watch a smooth universe become a web. The isosurface is the same marching-cubes code the fluid pages use.

Ships gain a pitch axis and an altitude and dogfight in three dimensions under a 3D pursuit AI, banking into turns, rendered with Three.js under a free camera. The 3D flight model is a strict superset of the 2D one -- at pitch 0 it reduces exactly to the old game -- and esBox3d runs in opt-in fly3d mode, so the 2D game and the planar-fight 3D VIEW page (es-box3d-3d.html) are unchanged. ship-ship collision is now a 3D SLAB (v3832): box3d's own footprint is dormant and an altitude-band collider is the authority, so two ships ram only when their footprints AND altitudes overlap -- vertically clear ships pass freely, and box3d's altitude-blind planar push is gone. The response rides box3d's velocity for x-z and the flight model's altitude for the vertical; full volumetric box3d contact-filtering is still a WASM round. Ships wear Slug outline-text nameplates (class + live hull%, sized by distance from one atlas with no re-bake) on an overlay surface -- the first adoption of the v3823 Slug renderer in a real scene. The backdrop is now a baked nebula/star SKYBOX (v3833): a seedable gradient+noise generator bakes a six-face cubemap whose colour is a pure function of direction, so the faces are seamless by construction; the old flat fill and 700-point starfield are gone and the stars are baked in. Ships trail SWEPT-SPINE ENGINE TRAILS (v3834): one static mesh whose every vertex is placed in the vertex shader from a per-ship spine data texture (a ship's recent path resampled at fixed arc length with a rotation-minimizing frame), so a long trail and a short one cost the same buffer -- technique reimplemented from Noniv/snowflow_demo's surf wake, nothing vendored. A PROCEDURAL STAR (v3835) hangs at the key-light direction, its photosphere baked from the SAME gradient+noise generator as the skybox (granulation + a temperature colour) with limb darkening and a corona applied in the shader. THE PLANET'S SURFACE IS CUBE-BAKED (v3842): the same seeded terrain is baked into a cubemap rather than an equirectangular texture -- so it spends its texels evenly instead of ~80x more densely on the poles than the equator, and the faces meet seamlessly by construction -- and the bake now carries a normal map derived from the height field's own tangent-plane gradient, a roughness mask (smooth seas, rough land) and the height itself, read back on the CPU to displace the sphere so the silhouette carries the terrain too (the Relief button toggles both halves). THE SCENE IS POPULATED (v3843, the Structures button): an ASTEROID BELT whose rocks are icospheres displaced by the planet's own fbm3 and placed by rejection so no two interpenetrate, and a GREEBLED STATION -- hull modules along a spine wearing plates from a recursive panel split that PARTITIONS each face exactly (areas sum, nothing overlaps, nothing escapes), drawn as one instanced mesh for ~900 plates. SHIPS THROW DEBRIS WHEN HIT (v3844, the Hit FX button), ported from cockpit.html's VFX: the burst is chosen from the shield state AFTER absorption, so shields up throws a small cyan spark shower, shields gone throws a bigger red one, and a kill adds a third amber burst ON TOP of the second -- cockpit's own rule, graded against a transcription of its hit() over 3600 shield/armour/damage combinations. Unlike the source it uses no Math.random and decays per SECOND rather than per frame, so the spray does not travel further on a faster machine. A FOLD/WARP JUMP TUNNEL (v3836, the Jump button) sweeps the spine tube down a curving fold path viewed from inside, its ring pattern scrolling toward the camera via a stateless fract wrap (the endless-loop trick, not a persistent buffer) and ramped in and out by a jump envelope. Compressible Euler -- the solver for the flows the lattice is measurably wrong for. Dump energy into a point and stand back: the shock radius grows as the square root of time, an answer exact since the 1940s and written nowhere in this code. The page fits that exponent live while it runs, so you can watch one half appear out of nothing but a hot spot and the Euler equations. The other button turns two layers over -- heavy resting on light -- and gravity refuses the arrangement. Euler has no viscosity and no diffusivity anywhere in it, so the interface between them stays sharp and the mushrooms keep their edges. Colour is temperature, on the same blackbody ramp the lava wears.

The compressible Euler kernel was written on a machine with no GPU, so this page is the check, and it runs on your hardware. It has a better test available than the lattice adjudicator did: a strong shock compresses gas by exactly (gamma+1)/(gamma-1), which is 6.000 at gamma 1.4 -- an answer known since Rankine and Hugoniot in the 1870s and written nowhere in the kernel. So the GPU is not merely asked to agree with the CPU; it is asked to find that number alone. There is a sabotage button that makes the kernel's equation of state 2% wrong, so you can watch the check go red.

pages.d: Every WGSL kernel here ships a tolerance earned from a floor measured on one machine and doubled. The fleet has been accumulating the same measurement from real silicon in every submitted bench report, and nothing was reading it. This does: worst measured gap per adapter per kernel, with the margin that tolerance actually has on that device. Float gaps and the zero-tolerance integer spin count are kept in separate columns and never pooled, because the aggregate an atlas naturally wants to compute is the meaningless one.

A running fluid wearing a skin made of its own X-ray shadows. The physics is SPH, and its kernel is the blobulator's kernel -- metaballs picked it in 1986 for looking like wax, fluid dynamics picked it in 2003 for being smooth and compact, and they are the same function. So the fluid's sinogram is closed-form: written down exactly, never integrated. The scanner gathers its views one per frame while the fluid keeps moving, so the smear you see is real, not an effect -- and it is worst when the fluid moves by about its own structure size during the scan, which is why real CT scanners are fast and patients hold their breath. Momentum is conserved to 1.6e-15, the kernel integrates to 1 to fourteen decimals, and a particle lattice recovers a density nobody told it.

One glyph outline morphing into the next through vendor/morphicons and drawn by Slug: the quadratic contours become an SVG path, morphicons pairs and interpolates the subpaths, and each frame packs one glyph into its own atlas. The melt mode fills the glyph with the Doom Fire and melts it to a puddle on the baseline, the fill riding along. Gated by tools/ship/slugMorph-selfcheck.mjs and tools/ship/slugMelt-selfcheck.mjs.

Slug outline text rotated on screen and laid on a plane in perspective through gfx/device.js on either backend: the shipped SlugDilate keeps its half-pixel edge under a varying w, held by tools/ship/slugProjective-selfcheck.mjs. Drag the sliders.

Slug text cost on THIS machine's GPU: a wall of glyphs per face at five sizes and three squashes, timed by GPU timestamps where the device was granted them, beside the atlas's own curves-per-band statistics -- the numbers the band-count question needs before anybody tunes one.

The first on-GPU draw of the Slug outline-text renderer merged at v3823: one quadratic TrueType font is packed into a curve texture and a band texture once, then the same data is drawn at eight sizes from 8px to a wall-filling title with no atlas to rebuild and no size-dependent baking, because the fragment shader reads the actual Bezier control points and solves for coverage per pixel. The Cross-check button reads the framebuffer back and compares coverage against slugEval.slugRender at matching points -- the check the library's note left open. Font: IBM Plex Serif (SIL OFL 1.1). A 3-D ticker of Slug outline glyphs as Box3D rigid bodies: one box per glyph dropped onto a conveyor, tumbling and wrapping, each drawn through gfx/device.js with its own body matrix on either backend. The plumbing is gated by tools/ship/slugTicker-selfcheck.mjs. The napalm mode (?mode=napalm) draws the bodies through the Doom Fire fill and drops a trail of fire puddles on the floor behind each, fading by age, gated by tools/ship/slugNapalm-selfcheck.mjs. The shatter button bursts the centre glyph into nine box3d shards each carrying its sub-rectangle of the glyph, gated by tools/ship/slugShatter-selfcheck.mjs.
An audio file wrapped onto a globe: time goes round it, frequency runs pole to pole, loudness is height, silence is sea. A pure tone is a ring; a rising sweep is a spiral.

The front door for the statistical-mechanics arc: the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution, the Planck law, the Debye heat capacity, Bose-Einstein condensation, the degenerate Fermi gas, the Sackur-Tetrode entropy, the finite-temperature chemical potential that ties the three statistics together, and the paramagnet's Schottky anomaly (localised spins -- ising.js without the interactions). Eight graded modules that had no door at all -- runnable only by typing a selfcheck path (seven found this page at v3818, the paramagnet at v3820). The page computes nothing itself: every figure comes from a module under physics/ with its own gate, and the headline of each panel is the KEY that module is graded on. The chemical-potential panel is the one to look at: one density constraint sets the fugacity for all three gases, mu = kT ln z, and the classical answer falls out of both quantum ones as the gas thins.

The Steam Deck as a full SweK peer: an x86_64 Linux box that runs ai-bridge/server.js itself rather than a subset, joins the UDP 47474 fleet beacon and can host the GPU brain. Honest about the half that has never been verified -- no physical Deck has ever run this, so the RDNA2 GPU rows, SteamOS's read-only root and Game Mode are reasoned from Valve's documentation rather than measured, while the server, beacon, mDNS and port-takeover rows were measured on generic x86_64 Linux.

Turn the polytropic index and watch a star's density profile change shape -- and its surface run away to infinity as the index approaches 5. Three indices have exact closed forms and the page draws them over the integration so you can see the solver land on them; past n=5 the star has no edge at all, which is why Chandrasekhar used it as the boundary of physical polytropes.
Install and run the Sunshine game-stream HOST, and launch Moonlight V+ on a phone over adb. The host half of the phone-as-a-screen story.

Paste an SVG and forge it into a 3D metal medal/badge: its paths are parsed and bevel-extruded, holes and inner points preserved (the vector counterpart to the raster sprite-loft). Controls for thickness, bevel, color and metalness; orbit to inspect. Parsing is pinned by svgExtrudeCore-selfcheck. For faction insignia, achievement medals, and 3D UI ornaments.

The ship's computer scanning a target: a Sobel edge pass turns the ship sprite into an LCARS vector schematic, a scan line sweeps down and lights the outline, a reticle frames it, and a readout shows hull/shield/weapon. Works on our 2D sprites today -- no 3D model needed.

In 2D the set of cells whose gradient cannot be determined from cell averages is exactly two, forever. In 3D it is 6n - it grows linearly with the mesh, tracking the box edges rather than its faces, so refinement makes the defect rarer and more numerous at the same time.

The thermal lattice, made visible. A second distribution carries heat the way the first carries momentum, and one line couples them: hot fluid is lighter. Heat a layer from below and nothing happens -- the heat just conducts through -- until the Rayleigh number crosses 1708, and then the fluid organises itself into rolls. Nothing in the code contains that number; drag the slider across it and watch it decide. Or turn the layers over -- heavy resting on light -- and gravity refuses the arrangement: the interface goes unstable and overturns into mushrooms. The colour is the temperature, on the same blackbody ramp the lava uses, because here the heat really is the material.

Rayleigh-Benard convection in three dimensions: a layer heated from below organising itself into plumes, hot columns rising and cold sheets falling. Nothing tells it to. The surfaces are isosurfaces of temperature, marched fresh from the live field, and here the blackbody ramp is honestly reading heat -- unlike the duct, where it reads speed and says so. The Mach gauge matters: this engine measured its own lattice's Galilean error and wrote down a rule -- trust it below Mach 0.1. Push the Rayleigh slider hard enough and the page will tell you when you have broken the engine's own rule, because a demo that quietly runs outside its verified range is a lie with nice colours.

Fetches a named three version from the npm registry in the browser, imports its WebGPU build beside the vendored 0.178, renders one TSL gradient with each and reads it back: whether the newer build runs on THIS machine's Chrome, with the exact error when it does not. Save the JSON as tools/ship/three-probe.json.

A CT scanner, owned rather than imported. The shadows are not simulated -- the Radon transform of an ellipse is closed-form, so the sinogram on the left is written down exactly, and it was checked against a brute-force line integral to 1.57e-5 before anything reconstructed anything. Filtered back-projection then recovers the object from those shadows alone, converging to 0.06% away from edges as the angle count rises. Drag the angle slider and watch a smear become a head. The volume it produces is a 3D scalar field, so the same marching cubes that draws the D3Q19 wake and the cosmic web draws this too -- reconstruction was never a rendering problem for this engine.

A TOROIDAL DEFORM BUFFER driving a real-time wave simulation on a curved surface (v3837). An N x N field is addressed with wraparound (modulo) indexing, so it has no edges -- a ripple leaving one side re-enters the other, the domain is periodic, and scrolling the read origin moves the whole field under the viewport with no buffer copy. Because a wrapped grid IS a torus topologically, the field maps onto a torus with no seam and the waves chase themselves around it. The 2D wave equation runs on the CPU here (leapfrog, wraparound 5-point Laplacian, CFL-safe); the GPU ping-pong-texture version is the optimisation. Drops splat with toroidal wrap; Scroll demonstrates the moving window; Reset stills the field. Answer-key gate: toroidalField-selfcheck (wraparound indexing, the cross-seam energy transfer, CFL stability, scroll==shift, seamless torus map).
A 3D voxel render of BiglyBT torrents: each tower is a download, lit cubes are progress, color is state, glow is speed.

pages.d: On a square the offset from cell centre to furthest evaluation point is exactly half the lever the gradient was built on. On a triangle it is sqrt(5/2) = 1.5811 - above one - so the escape is forced by geometry rather than by the limiter, and only the centroid conserves.

Diffusion is the process that smooths everything, and Turing showed it can DESTABILISE a uniform state into stripes when the inhibitor diffuses faster than the activator. The Brusselator is used because its algebra is exact: the threshold B_c = (1 + A sqrt(Du/Dv))^2 is closed form and the simulation is never told it. Below it every mode decays however long you wait.
Spinning voxel globe; zoom from orbit to a local geological strata view.

The cap on SweK's voxelize path: a voxel volume becomes a watertight triangle mesh you can spin, and export as OBJ. Pick a shape or crank the resolution -- the same voxelsToMesh() runs on the filter-series page voxels too, so content -> voxels -> mesh -> asset.

pages.d: An opt-in front door to schildep/verified-polygon-intersection (MIT): a multipolygon intersection algorithm written and machine-checked in Lean 4, compiled to WebAssembly, with a browser demo you draw two multipolygons on and see the proved intersection computed live. NOTHING OF THEIRS IS VENDORED into this tree or imported into this engine's process -- the button fetches the four prebuilt static files GitHub Pages already serves (index.html, lean_app.js, lean_app.wasm, coi-serviceworker.min.js) onto THIS machine, pinned to a reviewed commit, and this server serves them back with real Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy headers -- upstream's own service worker exists only because GitHub Pages cannot set HTTP headers; this server can, so it does, without touching a byte of their files.
DOOM WAD map viewer — load a .wad and explore the level geometry.

Two rounds measured zero-Neumann producing a wrong answer and said the assertion was what was false. Here is a field where it is true: on the wall that really is a zero-flux wall it is exact, free and rank-restoring - and on the next wall along it is worse than doing nothing.

A star map that clusters because a power spectrum put the structure there, not because anyone drew it. The field comes from makeGRF -- white noise filtered by the square root of a prescribed P(k), whose measured spectrum comes back at 1.006 of what was asked for over twelve universes -- and the stars are Poisson-sampled from it. Toggle SCATTER to see the same star count with no field behind it: a pure scatter has variance exactly equal to its mean, which is what Poisson means, and it measures 1.0. The clustered map measures well above that, and the excess is structure. Chopping a smooth field into countable stars costs exactly V/N in shot noise, predicted before the code runs. Click any star to warp to it.

Kingdom-style 2D water on gfx/device.js in both shader languages: two seeded displacement maps scrolled at two speeds and by the pointer's x over a parallax divider, their sum displacing the scene sample, a tint curved by the sample's greyness, and foam where both channels pass a threshold. After StefanJo3107/2D-Water-Shader (MIT), read and hand-written. Held texel for texel and mask for mask to a CPU twin by tools/ship/water2d-selfcheck.mjs.

A hollow metal pipe carries nothing below its cutoff frequency. TE and TM modes come from the same 2D eigenproblem differing only in a boundary condition, and that difference decides which mode is dominant: solving TM with the wrong condition returns a tidy, plausible cutoff for a pipe that does not exist. The mode SET is what catches it, not the frequencies.

A PERSISTENT TOROIDAL ACCUMULATION BUFFER following a ship (v3838) -- the snowflow deform buffer proper, the persistent half the stateless wave could not do. An N x N field is world-locked by wraparound addressing so it covers a size x size window that FOLLOWS the ship without ever being copied; the ship stamps wear/scorch into it every frame and it DECAYS, so a trail smears behind and heals over time. The subtle part, gated in wearField-selfcheck: the SCROLL-AND-CLEAR -- when the window recenters, only the newly-exposed texels (world the ship has just reached) are zeroed, while everything still in the window keeps accumulating; clearing everything would erase the trail, clearing nothing would ghost the world you left and returned to. The buffer runs on the CPU here; the GPU ping-pong-texture version is the optimisation. Pause/Reset/Heal. Answer-key gate: wearField-selfcheck (toroidal addressing, accumulation, persistence across scroll, re-entry clearing, decay).

So the exposure is stated plainly and warned on before every start rather than silently narrowed by running a fork of their behaviour.
